questions.question: According to the Indian Bureau of mines 2020, which two states of India have the maximum gold ore reserves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar and Rajasthan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gold **in its purest form is a ***bright, slightly reddish yellow, dense, soft malleable, and ductile metal***.
 
• It is one of the **least reactive chemical elements **and is solid *under standard conditions*.
 
• **Gold **often occurs in **free elemental (native) **form, as *nuggets or grains, in rocks, in veins, and alluvial deposits*.
 
• **Gold dissolves **in an **alkaline solution of cyanide**, which is used in mining and electroplating.
 
• **Gold** is **resistant **to **corrosion **and to **most acids **and has unique properties distinct from other metals.
 
• By States, the largest resources in terms of gold ore (primary) are located in **Bihar (44%)** followed by **Rajasthan (25%), Karnataka (21%), West Bengal &

 Andhra Pradesh (3% each)** and **Jharkhand (2%).**
 
• The remaining **2%** resources of ore are located in ***Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Kerala, Maharashtra

 , and Tamil Nadu.***
 
• Although, **Bihar **is the **leading State in India **as far as resources of **gold ore **are concerned.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __**Indian Bureau of Mines:**__

 
• The Indian Bureau of Mines was set up on **1st March 1948**.
 
• Initially **IBM **functioned **purely** as an **advisory body**.
 
• It helped the government in framing various rules like **Mines & Minerals (Regulation & Development) Act, 1948, Mineral Concession Rules, 1949, and Petroleum Concession Rules, 1949**.
 
• **IBM **was given a set of functions in **1950 **and by it, the inspection of mines and mineral prospects became a regular activity.
 
• By **1953 IBM **was given an additional function of undertaking detailed exploration of mineral deposits.
 
• Among the minerals explored by **IBM **were ***Iron Ore, Limestone, Dolomite, Coal, Copper, and Tungsten.***
 
• Later **Mineral Conservation & Development Rules,1955, and Mining Leases (Modification of Terms),1956 **were framed.
 
• An **ore dressing laboratory **was set up in **Delhi **in **1955**.

questions.question: ‘The Trophic-Dynamic Aspect of Ecology’ was studied by whom in the year 1942?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raymond L Lindeman.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__A trophic-dynamic aspect of ecology:__

__
 
• The fundamental process by which energy moves from one trophic level to the next in an ecosystem is known as trophic dynamics.

Energy flow in the ecosystem:__

__
 
• In a food chain, the energy flow follows the 10 percent law.
 
• According to this law, only 10 percent of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the other; the rest is lost into the atmosphere.
 
• This energy is stored in various organic products in the plants from the sun via the process of photosynthesis.
 
• This is then passed on to the primary consumers in the food chain when the herbivores consume (primary consumers) the plants as food.
 
• Then conversion of chemical energy stored in plant products into kinetic energy occurs, degradation of energy will occur through its conversion into heat.
 
• The energy flow is: Primary (100%) → First level/ Primary (10%) → Second-level/ Secondary (1%) → Third level / Tertiary (0.1%).
 
• The energy flow in the ecosystem is clearly unidirectional.
 
• The ten percent rule of transfer of energy from one trophic level to the next is being credited to Raymond Lindeman (1942).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Arthur Tansley:

 
• It was in 1935 that Arthur Tansley, the British ecologist, coined the term 'ecosystem'.
 
• It is the interactive system established between the biocoenosis (the group of living creatures), and their biotope, the environment in which they live.

Ernst Haeckel:

 
• The word “Ecology” was coined by “Ernst Haeckel”.
 
• It is the branch of biology that studies organizations in their environment.
 
• Ecology word is taken from the Greek word Oekologie, Oikos meaning “House” and logos meaning “Study”.
 
• Ecology is the study of the household.
 
• Ernst Haeckel also proposed the theory of development and evolution.

Charles Elton:

 
• The concept of the ecological pyramid was first proposed by Charles Elton in 1927.
 
• It was known as the Eltonian pyramid then. E.P. Odum wrote the popular ecology book 'Fundamentals of Ecology' in 1953.

questions.question: The Plan for Partition of India is known as the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3rd June Plan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__Mountbatten Plan(1947) or 3rd June Plan:__

__
 
• The failure of the Cabinet Mission was followed by the collapse of the interim Government. 
 
• By the end of 1946 communal violence increased in the country and the British feared that India would settle for a civil war.
 
• Lord Mountbatten replaced Lord Wavell as Viceroy of India in 1947.
 
• Mountbatten's formula was to divide India and at the same time retain the maximum possible unity. 
 
• The actual division between the two new dominions of India and Pakistan was accomplished to be known as the 3rd June Plan.
 
• It was announced at a press conference by Mountbatten on 4 June 1947, and the date of Independence was announced- 15 August 1947.
 
• The main points of the plan were:
 
 
• **Partition**: Muslim-dominated areas may be separated to form a Dominion.
 
 
• Referendum for NWEP and Sylhet: The fate of North-West Frontier Province and Sylhet district of Bengal was to be decided by a referendum.
 
• India would be free by 15 August 1947.
 
• Independence of princely states was ruled out.
 
• A boundary commission to be set up in case of partition.
 
• The Muslim league's demand for a separate state was thus conceded.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Wavell plan/Shimla Conference (1945):

 
 
• It was named after the Viceroy of India, Lord Wavell. 
 
• A few proposals in this plan are:
 
 
• With the exception of the Viceroy and Commander in Chief, all the members of the Viceroy's executive council will be Indians.
 
• A kind of interim government was suggested.
 
• Transfer of foreign affairs portfolio from the Governor-General to an Indian member
 
• Congress rejected the Wavell plans because of the actions of the Muslim league.
 
 
 
 
 
• August Offer (1940):
 
 
• On 8th August Lord Linlithgow suggested some measures to get the support of the INC and Muslim League for World War II that is known as August Offer or Linlithgow's offer.
 
• Immediate expansion of the Viceroy Executive Council by including more number of Indians.
 
• A war advisory council
 
• Constitution-making body after the war.
 
• All the constitutional agreements in India must take the consensus of the minority community (veto power to the Muslim League).
 
• Congress rejected the August Offer.
 
 
 
• Poona Pact (1932):
 
 
• It was an agreement between Gandhi and Ambedkar.
 
• Madan Mohan Malviya signed the pact on behalf of Gandhi.
 
• According to this pact:
 
 
• Separate electorates were replaced by the joint electorates for depressed classes.
 
• As against 71 seats announced by MacDonald, this pact reserved 148 seats in the Provincial legislature.
 
• About 18% of the total seats were also reserved for the pressed classes in the central legislature.

questions.question: How do colours contribute to effective presentation and documents in MS PowerPoint?

options.text: Colours help in copying and pasting content between documents
Colours create a sense of hierarchy and emphasise important information.
Colours make the content appear larger and more prominent.
Automatically correct spelling and grammar errors in the text.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Colours create a sense of hierarchy and emphasize important information.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Colors have an impact on the way we see and interpret visual information.
 
• They can influence emotion, set the mood, build structure and, emphasize certain elements.
 
• This means that choosing the right colors can make your presentation stand out and control how it’s received.
 
• Colors are often associated with emotions.
 
• Warm colors, like reds, oranges, and yellows can be used to communicate energy, excitement, optimism, and enthusiasm.
 
• In contrast, cool colors such as blues, greens, and violets lend feelings of professionalism, dependability, and elegance. 
 
• One key rule in the use of color theory for presentations is to keep colors simple and balanced.
 
• Choose a palette of no more than three colors (black and white don’t count as colors for this purpose).
 
• Another rule for balancing the proportions of colors in presentation and design is called the 60-30-10 rule.
 
• According to this rule, once you have chosen your three colors, you should use the primary color for 60% of the space on the slides.
 
• The secondary color for 30% of the space, and the accent color for 10% of the space.

questions.question: Which of the following Legislative Bills proposed to set-up the Indian Antarctic Authority (IAA) under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 is legislation related to the activities of the Indian Antarctic Program, which is under the purview of the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
 
• The Ministry of Earth Sciences is responsible for providing services related to weather, climate, ocean, and coastal states, as well as for exploration and research in polar regions.
 
• The bill also aims to give effect to the Antarctic Treaty, the Convention on the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources, and the Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty.
 
• The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 introduced in Lok Sabha aims at providing national measures to protect the Antarctic environment and the dependent and associated ecosystems.
 
• The Indian Antarctic Bill will also be useful in building credibility and enhancing the status of the country globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Ministry of Law and Justice is responsible for formulating and implementing laws and policies related to the legal system in India.

 
• The Ministry of External Affairs is responsible for managing India's foreign relations and diplomacy.
 
• The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is responsible for the welfare and development of tribal communities in India.
 
• Hence, the statement "The Indian Antarctic Bill, 2022 belongs to the Ministry of India."

questions.question: What is in situ conservation method of biodiversity?

options.text: It concerns with the conservation of species in botanic gardens and captive breeding programmes.
It concerns with the conservation areas as ‘warehouses’ of biological information.
It concerns with the cryopreservation of gametes.
It concerns with the protective maintenance of threatened species in zoological parks.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It concerns with the conservation areas as ‘warehouses’ of biological information**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **In situ conservation** is a method of conservation wherein efforts are directed to **preserve species in their natural habitats** where they occur.
 
• It is considered the best way of biodiversity conservation and includes the establishment of **national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, reserved and protected forests, and wetlands**.
 
• This is because it **allows the ongoing process of evolution and adaptation within their environments**.
 
• The goal of in situ conservation is to **maintain healthy and natural populations of species in the wild**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ex-situ conservation**, which translates to "**off-site conservation**," is a strategy of biodiversity preservation where various species are conserved **outside their natural habitats**.
 
• These methods include **zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, DNA banks, breeding programs**, and in vitro plant tissue and cell cultures among others.
 
• These facilities **provide suitable living conditions and care** to ensure the survival and reproduction of species.
 
• For instance, botanical gardens maintain collections of endangered plants for research and education.
 
• Seed banks play a crucial role in ex-situ conservation as they store diverse genetic material, allowing us to preserve and reintroduce species in case of loss in the wild due to environmental changes, disease, or human influence.
 
• Animal breeding programs involve carefully planned pairings to increase population size while maintaining genetic diversity.
 
• **Options 1, 3, and 4 are a part of the ex-situ conservation strategy**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a collection of authoritative terminology originally compiled from IUPAC recommendations published by the scientific divisions of the union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold Book**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **IUPAC Gold Book** is a compilation of **authoritative terminology that was originally collated from IUPAC recommendations published by the scientific divisions of the union**.
 
• This book is a critical resource for **scientific vocabulary and definitions used by the scientific community, particularly in the field of chemistry**.
 
• IUPAC, the **International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry**, is an international federation that represents chemists in individual countries and strives to promote global scientific activity.
 
• The Gold Book is one of many color books published by IUPAC, each serving a different purpose in the field of chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Red Book**: Also referred to as "**Nomenclature of Inorganic Chemistry**," the Red Book provides recommendations for the naming of **inorganic compounds**.

questions.question: What is the horizontal field view of one eye in human beings?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **The human eye** is like **a camera**. Its lens system forms an image on a light-sensitive screen called the **retina**.
 
• The **eyeball** is approximately spherical in shape with a **diameter of about 2.3 cm**.
 
• The **eye lens** forms an** inverted real image** of the object on the **retina**.
 
• The** light-sensitive cells** get activated upon** illumination and generate electrical signals**. These signals are sent to the brain via the optic nerves. The brain interprets these signals, and finally, processes the information so that we perceive objects as they are. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When** the light** is very **bright**, the** iris** contracts the** pupil** to allow** less light to enter**
 
• However, in **dim light**, the** iris expands **the pupil to **allow more light to enter**
 
• Thus, the** pupil opens** completely through the relaxation of the iris.
 
• **A human being has a horizontal field of view of about 150° with one eye **and about 180° with two eyes. **Hence option 1 is correct. **

options.text: There are 18 periods and 7 groups in the periodic table.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **There are 18 periods and 7 groups in the periodic table.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the Modern Periodic Table, there is 18 vertical columns called Groups and 7 horizontal rows called Periods.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__** 
 __
 
• Hence, the 1st statement is incorrect and 3rd statement is correct. 
 
 
 
• Group 1 elements are called Alkali Metals and Group 2 elements are known as Alkaline Earth Metals, hence statement 2 is correct.
 
• Noble or Inert Gases are placed in **Group 18**, hence statement 4 is **correct**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The modern periodic table** is a tabular arrangement of the **chemical elements**, organized by their **atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties**.
 
• It was first developed by Russian chemist** Dmitri Mendeleev** in **1869**, and has since been expanded and refined by numerous scientists.
 
• The table is divided into** rows called periods** and **columns called groups or families**.
 
• Elements in the** same group** have **similar chemical properties**, while elements in the **same period** have the **same number of electron shells**.
 
• The periodic table currently contains **118 confirmed elements**, with additional elements being discovered and added over time.
 
• The elements are organized based on their **atomic structure**, with the** number of protons in the nucleus** determining an element's identity.
 
• The table is a powerful tool for understanding the **relationships between different elements **and predicting their** chemical behavior**.
 
• It provides a framework for organizing and studying the properties of elements, as well as for understanding their roles in chemical reactions and compounds.
 
• The periodic table is widely used in chemistry, physics, biology, and other scientific fields.
 
• It has also been influential in the development of new materials and technologies, as well as in the study of the universe and the natural world.
 
• The periodic table has undergone several revisions and updates over the years, reflecting advances in scientific knowledge and the discovery of new elements.
 
• Elements are classified into different categories on the periodic table, including** metals, nonmetals, metalloids, alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, transition metals, halogens, and noble gases**.
 
• The table also includes** lanthanides and actinides,** which are often placed separately at the bottom to conserve space.

questions.question: Which of the following programmes was initiated in 1979 with the objective of upgrading the traditional skills of rural youth belonging to families living below the poverty line, with family income below ₹3,500 per year?

• At** least half of the overall beneficiaries should be women**.
 
• The amount of rural youth moving to urban regions may be reduced because it was producing activities in the rural areas.

• creating durable assets for strengthening the infrastructure so as to meet the growing requirements of the rural economy.
